newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ready to cooperate with IMF on Thai woes-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan ready to cooperate with IMF on Thai woes-MOF.

text.p: Japan will cooperate with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) if necessary to cope with economic woes faced by Thailand and other Asian countries, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.

Asked if Japan had any detailed ideas on what it would do for Asian currency stability, Mitsuzuka said: "We will tackle this issue on discussion with the IMF. We must keep watch over the market situation and analyse it by keeping close contact with other countries. If necessary, we will likely cooperate with the IMF."
Mitsuzuka said he supported Thailand's decision to switch to a managed floating system for the baht and he thought the baht would stabilise.

He said he would listen to Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya's explanation of the situation concerning the baht and Thailand's economy when Thanong visits Tokyo this week. Japan will decide details after that, he said.
"There are analyses that the Asian currency situation will stabilise. There are also various views being expressed in the market. There may be a gap between that and the reality," he said.
Asked about the impact of Asian currency turmoil on the yen, Mitsuzuka said: "I don't know. The yen is being traded every day, while reflecting economic fundamentals."
